research_rationale: EO 6221-B (July 26, 1933) is not a section 3 code approval. It records an agreement by the Conference Committee of the National Association of Hosiery Manufacturers to be bound by certain articles of its proposed code "pending the approval of a Code of Fair Competition", offered under "Section 4" and expressly "subject to cancellation or modification at any time without notice". Section 4(a) agreements are a category the reviewed shared analysis does not decide, so the repeal end cannot be applied by rule.

Its page record is a Common Crawl capture of 2024-12-04T12:59:10Z whose heading names Executive Order 6257, whose date (August 19, 1933) and subject agree with the text, and whose text sha256 equals the held text's. savings_reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the approved Code of Fair Competition for the Photographic Manufacturing Industry before June 14, 1935 are accrued consequences that the repeal did not turn into continuing commands; nothing in S.J. Res. 113 (SUPPLEMENT:SJRES113) continues the approval after June 14, 1935. Any antitrust exemption for complying action before the repeal (NIRA section 5, SUPPLEMENT:NIRA5) is likewise an accrued effect; the resolution's proviso, which extends the exemption only to "agreements and action thereunder" meeting stated conditions, leaves open how far it narrowed the exemption for past action, so the claim records no continuing exemption and no surviving approval. A committee actually created under condition (1) and any members chosen or appointed for it are accrued consequences of the order; this claim records no continuing command to create or maintain the committee.
earlier_end_check: The approval is "subject to the following condition" (1), a committee requirement with no period, "until" date or provisional approval; the order states no end of its own. Searched the held order texts (jobs/*/output/texts, through the Cruden lookup and a follow-up regex search on the code's name), the census register and the WPA 1944 list for later orders citing EO 6257 by number or naming its code: no held order text cites this order by number and no other held text names the code, so nothing earlier than the repeal is established. No held record shows this code cancelled, modified under section 10(b), superseded, revoked or suspended before June 14, 1935. June 16, 1935 is not an end: section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 replaced the original two-year expiry with April 1, 1936.
scope_check: Two clauses: the lead approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Photographic Manufacturing Industry (chars 740-1141) and condition (1) (chars 1143-1704) requiring an industry committee. The order states no other condition, exception, stay or exemption.
independent_command_check: The only command beside the approval is condition (1): that "a Photographic Manufacturing Industry Committee be created to cooperate with the Administrator as a Planning and Fair Practice Agency for the Photographic Manufacturing Industry", consisting of seven industry representatives and "three members without vote appointed by the Administrator". Section 3(a) of Title I (SUPPLEMENT:NIRA3) lets the President impose conditions "as a condition of his approval of any such code", and the order states this requirement as a condition of its approval, citing only Title I and the general words "and otherwise"; it names no other statute, so it is not a separate appointment or delegation under another authority. No held record shows the committee created, its members elected or appointed, or the committee dissolved, so no performance date or earlier end is claimed. The condition is recorded as a term of the approval that stopped operating with it; any committee actually formed, and any appointments made, are surviving consequences (see savings), not continuing commands of this order.
savings_check: Savings reviewed under NIRA section 5 and S.J. Res. 113 section 2 and its proviso: accrued acts, liabilities and any completed-action exemption under the Code of Fair Competition for the Photographic Manufacturing Industry are preserved as accrued effects; nothing continues the approval, and no held source shows a prosecution or enforcement continued after June 14, 1935. The committee condition leaves no continuing command; any committee formed and any appointments made are accrued consequences.

Any antitrust exemption for complying action before the repeal (NIRA section 5, SUPPLEMENT:NIRA5) is likewise an accrued effect; the resolution's proviso, which extends the exemption only to "agreements and action thereunder" meeting stated conditions, leaves open how far it narrowed the exemption for past action, so the claim records no continuing exemption and no surviving approval. Wages paid and acts done under the amended wage provisions before the repeal are accrued.
earlier_end_check: The order states no period, condition, "until" date or provisional approval of its own. Searched the held order texts (jobs/*/output/texts, through the Cruden lookup and a follow-up regex search on the code's name), the census register and the WPA 1944 list for later orders citing EO 6964B by number or naming its code: no held order text cites EO 6964-B by number and no later held text names this amended code; the earlier approval it amends is EO 6437 (November 17, 1933), a separate order outside this claim. No held record shows this code cancelled, modified under section 10(b), superseded, revoked or suspended before June 14, 1935. June 16, 1935 is not an end: section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 replaced the original two-year expiry with April 1, 1936.
scope_check: Three clauses after correction: the adoption of the National Industrial Recovery Board's report, the amendment order, the finding and the approval of the amended code (chars 409-1196); the replacement of Article V section 1 minimum wage rates by zone (chars 1462-2364); and the replacement of Article V section 5 weekly minimum wages by zone (chars 2366-2812). The opening authority paragraph (chars 0-409) recites authority and the basis for the report and commands nothing. The order states no condition, exception, stay or exemption.
independent_command_check: The order contains no appointment, direction to an agency, delegation under another statute or other command independent of the code; the "Approval Recommended" line records a recommendation of the National Industrial Recovery Board, not a command.
savings_check: Savings reviewed under NIRA section 5 and S.J. Res. 113 section 2 and its proviso: accrued acts, liabilities and any completed-action exemption under the Code of Fair Competition for the Paper and Pulp Industry are preserved as accrued effects; nothing continues the approval, and no held source shows a prosecution or enforcement continued after June 14, 1935.
